verdicts.note: Repeatedly self-identifies as a woman engineer; quote and context confirm female.
'Just a normal school' in answer to 'not an all-girls school' confirms mixed sex.
'Mechanical through and through' plus opening confirmation = Mechanical Engineering.
Seeing how things work/improving them attracted her = interesting work, agree.
Didn't want maths-only degree, chose broad engineering = maths/science without specialising.
'Broadest of all of them' supports varied-field appeal, agree.
'Where my strengths lie' plus grades steering her to maths/sci A-levels; thin but defensible, medium OK.
Says she knew what engineering was/what to expect, so disagree with 'little knowledge' is correct.
Has an uncle in industry but distant and doesn't know his field; her knowledge not from family = disagree, low conf appropriate.
Quote is more interest than challenge, but problem-solving appeal recurs ('good at problem solving','overcoming problems'); thin, low conf appropriate.
Switched to DIS course, named company, going on placement = yes.
Wants to apply engineering / work experience; she is part of the group she describes.
Repeated strong emphasis on applying theory vs lectures supports Strongly agree (5).
'Hopefully improve your grade at the end' = improve grades on return, agree.
Placement to help find a job after graduation, agree.
Expects placement skills to help choose final-year project, agree.
'Going to work and applying' gestures at experiencing real industry; thin but defensible, medium OK.
Excited to meet/work with new people and learn from the year = personal development.
'Pay wasn't really an issue... not the main incentive' = disagree money motivated her.
Extra DIS qualification; placement explicitly optional not compulsory, so 'other' (2) is correct.
Lecturers 'really good', support always there = satisfied with lecturer support.
Learnt to tolerate problems/work with people from group project = course develops interpersonal skills.
Describes skills as 'so varied' / 'diverse field' positively; expressed satisfaction thin but OK at medium.
Men more helpful because she's female, repeated at close = female students get more help, agree.
Names group project as 'worst'/'really difficult'; she also cites abstract advantages, so borderline vs neutral but dissatisfied defensible, low conf retained.
Cited quote is about career choices, but a direct 'Yeah' to 'pleased you chose this course' exists; code agree is correct, weak quote choice.
'Definitely some kind of design work' = design work specialism.
Explicitly undecided technical vs managerial = don't know.
'Would like to become a Chartered Engineer... what I'm aiming towards' = important.
Ambitious, wants to climb beyond basic engineering; maps to valuing promotion, medium OK.
Training opportunities a 'real bonus' in placement choice = training important.
Camaraderie among everyone influenced placement choice = people important.
Rejected a placement over hostile/male-dominated environment = work environment important.
